description: Traceability matrix of section 13.5: fixtures to contracts to tests to milestones. Two checks in InterCat.Architecture.Tests keep it honest.

fixtures.title: Seeded two-process TCP loopback exchange
fixtures.scenario: Section 13.1 scenario 1: TCP IPv4 loopback, several connections, several messages per connection.

truth.independence: Both processes write their own log from ordinary socket calls; neither reads InterCat state.

expected.note: The expected query bundle and its canonical hash are defined by IC-018. This milestone records measured counters and the inputs they came from.

environment.result: All six section 14.2 criteria met at 100%: 48 of 48 truth operations observed, bound to a flow instance and byte-measured, 0 false peer attributions of 4, 2 of 2 connections discovered and 4 of 4 memberships resolved. Truth and observed transport both 28,527 B sent. Tier TrafficVisualization, promoted once ADR-007 put this build in the section 1.3 matrix; the counters are unchanged from the first measured run.

environment.supportTier: Untested at the time of the run; ADR-007 later added this build
environment.result: All six section 14.2 criteria met; the tier stays ExperimentalEvidence because the build is outside the section 1.3 matrix.

fixtures.title: Local RPC calls to the Windows service control manager
fixtures.scenario: Section 13.1 scenario 5: local RPC with a known client, a Windows service host as the server, and the fixture run twice inside one capture.

truth.independence: The client logs every call it issues through the documented service API; it never reads InterCat state. The server is a Windows service host, which the scenario file states explicitly.

expected.note: 8 of 8 calls observed and bound to the expected interface with their completions paired, no byte domain on any descriptor, and no client-to-server peer paired. Tier ExperimentalEvidence; scope recorded in ADR-004.

environment.result: 8 of 8 truth calls observed, bound to the expected interface and completion-paired, reproduced across two runs in one capture. Tier ExperimentalEvidence on a supported build: the gaps are the source’s, not the build’s - no byte domain on any descriptor and no interface lifetime (ADR-004).

fixtures.title: Callback envelope admission, extended data and the elevated load series
fixtures.scenario: Sections 18.1-18.2: known metadata, an unknown schema with opaque bytes, known content under a metadata-only policy, header-only evidence, allowlisted and denied extended items, and a real EVENT_RECORD extended-data array read in bounded copies. The harness then drives a declared load series through both evidence variants, so the bounded queue reaches its limit and the writer becomes the pacing stage. The journal variant writes journal-v1; the format itself is FX-JOURNAL-002.

truth.independence: The corpus declares original bytes and policy inputs before admission; expected dispositions are stored separately.

expected.note: All four headers remain attributable. Only approved metadata survives; unknown and content bodies and a denied extended item have explicit omission outcomes; and an over-long extended item keeps its original length.

environment.result: Four five-level elevated series on a supported build: two writing the disposable probe format, on whose evidence ADR-008 was accepted, and two writing journal-v1 after the capture path moved to it. The journal-v1 call-stack series reports decisionReady: true with no blockers: identical ordered replay and an unchanged source clock at every level, 77,355 of 77,355 extended items copied, persisted and replayed, the queue bound reached with 60,006 counted drops and zero loss, and the writer pacing at 128% of an acquisition window in the clean series. journal-v1 costs 231 bytes per admitted record against the probe format's 327.

The portable admission policy round-trips admitted identity and extended items, excludes unapproved bodies and denied extended types, and rejects checksum corruption. The extended-data walker is asserted against a synthetic EVENT_RECORD, not against a live capture. The load series, its saturation classifier and the storage probe arithmetic are asserted portably; the elevated runs they describe are recorded under bench/results/.

provenance.contents: Synthetic headers, schemas, content markers, extended items, a synthetic EVENT_RECORD layout and expected policy dispositions.

fixtures.title: The frozen journal-v1 framing and its buffer ownership
fixtures.scenario: Sections 18.1 and 20.1: a fixed corpus of record envelopes written as a journal-v1 file, with a source clock frame, a schema and policy table, two batches, a retained body, a policy-omitted body, a truncated extended item, and a terminal frame. The clock frame is the file's own: a journal that names no clock, or two, is refused rather than read against an assumed one.

truth.independence: Every value in the corpus is fixed in the test, so the bytes it produces are decided by the format rather than by a run.

expected.note: The golden file is the contract. A change to the format changes these bytes, and changing this file is a deliberate act that needs an ADR.

environment.result: The corpus round-trips every field, a truncated file is refused as an interrupted capture, a flipped byte fails the per-record integrity check, another format major is refused, a journal with no clock frame or with two is refused, starting one never replaces existing evidence, and every pooled buffer is returned by the writer.

provenance.contents: Synthetic identifiers, header fields, extended items and body bytes. Nothing captured.
